_comment: DUMMY EXAMPLE DATA - This is a sample interview experience entry to demonstrate the expected file structure and format. Students should replace this with their actual interview experiences. Use the provided URLs format for assets: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPO/main/assets/YOUR_FILE.jpg
content: Cracked Google after 7 rounds of interviews. The process was tough but rewarding. Be prepared for a deep dive into data structures, algorithms, and system design. Googliness and culture fit are also very important.

rounds.description: Initial coding assessment over the phone.
questions: Given a list of numbers and a number k, return whether any two numbers from the list add up to k.
Explain the time and space complexity of your solution.

rounds.description: Follow-up coding assessment with a different interviewer.
questions: Given an array of integers, return a new array such that each element at index i of the new array is the product of all the numbers in the original array except the one at i.
What if you can't use division?

rounds.description: Whiteboard coding session focusing on core data structures.
questions: Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache.
Design a data structure that supports adding new words and finding if a string matches any previously added string.
Design a URL shortener service like TinyURL.
Discuss scalability, availability, and latency.

rounds.description: Coding problems related to multithreading and synchronization.
questions: Implement a thread-safe queue.
What is a deadlock and how would you prevent it?

rounds.description: Discussion about past projects and experiences.
questions: Tell me about a time you had a conflict with a team member.
Describe a challenging project you worked on and what you learned.

rounds.roundName: On-site Interview 5: Googliness and Culture Fit
rounds.description: Assessing cultural fit and general problem-solving skills.
questions: If you could be any Google product, which one would you be and why?
How would you improve Google Maps?

tips: Practice coding problems on a whiteboard.
Be able to articulate your thought process clearly.
Review system design concepts and be prepared to discuss trade-offs.
Prepare examples from your experience for behavioral questions.
Think about how you align with Google's values.

content: Meta's interview process is intense and focuses heavily on coding and system design. They value speed and accuracy. The behavioral round emphasizes their core values. Preparation is key to success.

rounds.description: Initial technical screening with coding problems.
questions: Implement a function to validate a binary search tree.
Design a data structure for a social network friend recommendation system.
Find the minimum window substring containing all characters.
Implement a graph algorithm to detect cycles.
Design an efficient algorithm for news feed ranking.
Solve a complex dynamic programming problem.
Design Instagram's backend architecture.
How would you handle billions of daily active users?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision.
How do you handle ambiguity in projects?

tips: Practice coding under time pressure.
Study Meta's core values thoroughly.
Focus on scalability in system design.
Be prepared to optimize your solutions.
Show passion for building impactful products.

content: Netflix has one of the most challenging interview processes. They look for senior-level thinking even in junior roles. Strong emphasis on system design, scalability, and real-world problem-solving. Culture fit is extremely important.

questions: Design a rate limiting system for API calls.
Implement an efficient caching mechanism.
Design an algorithm for video recommendation.
Optimize a solution for handling millions of concurrent streams.
Design a video streaming platform like Netflix.
How would you handle content delivery across the globe?
Design a microservices architecture for content management.
How would you ensure high availability and fault tolerance?
How do you embody Netflix's culture of freedom and responsibility?
Tell me about a time you made a high-impact decision.

tips: Study Netflix's tech blog extensively.
Understand their culture deck thoroughly.
Focus on scalability and performance.
Be prepared for senior-level discussions.
Show ownership and initiative in your examples.

content: Apple's interview process is thorough and focuses on both technical depth and product thinking. They value attention to detail and user experience. The process is long but well-structured. Strong fundamentals are essential.

questions: Implement a memory-efficient data structure.
Solve a problem related to iOS app optimization.
Design an efficient algorithm for image processing.
Implement a custom memory allocator.
Design the architecture for iCloud sync.
How would you optimize battery consumption in iOS apps?
How would you improve Siri's performance?
Design a feature for Apple Music.
Tell me about a time you paid attention to detail.
How do you approach user experience in your projects?

tips: Understand Apple's design philosophy.
Focus on performance and optimization.
Show passion for user experience.
Be prepared for product-related questions.
Demonstrate attention to detail in your answers.

content: Amazon SDE-2 role requires strong system design skills and leadership principles. Every answer must be backed by the STAR method. The bar is high, and they test both technical depth and breadth. Preparation is crucial.

questions: Design an efficient algorithm for warehouse optimization.
Implement a solution for order processing at scale.
Design Amazon's product recommendation engine.
Optimize a solution for real-time inventory management.
Design Amazon's order fulfillment system.
How would you handle Black Friday traffic?
Tell me about a time you delivered results under pressure.
Describe a situation where you had to dive deep into a problem.
Give an example of when you disagreed and committed.
How do you ensure customer obsession in your work?

tips: Master all 16 Leadership Principles with examples.
Practice system design for e-commerce scenarios.
Use STAR method for all behavioral questions.
Focus on scalability and cost optimization.
Show ownership and bias for action.
